CAVEAT WORTH NAMING (the finding acknowledges this in its last [I_strong] fact): the "IMAGE_FILE_DLL clear" bit is decisive for the Windows OS loader's LoadLibrary/CreateProcess paths, but a manual-mapper (which is how CLAUDE.md FK-10 §168 and S131 describe runtime.dll living in the game process at 0x7FFCA1400000) NEVER inspects Characteristics — it just maps sections and jumps. So "PE headers say EXE" tells you how Windows would treat it if launched normally, but does not prove that the S177 companion-process spawn actually happened via a real CreateProcessW call vs. some other mechanism. The static PE headers are CONSISTENT with the S177 finding, not PROOF of it — the S177 ETW capture with its own EPROCESS and parent PID is what carries that half. refuted_facts: Fact 2 [I_strong] — timing incompatibility argument uses the WRONG latency. The finding cites 'companion spawn latency ~50.05s' from S177 flight 7 (game-start to companion-start). But S177 doc line 164 explicitly records flight 9's spawn at t+5.0s from watcher-start after a fresh DR install, and states 'The trigger appears to be the DR install event itself'. So the actual TRIGGER→SPAWN latency is ~5s, not 50s. FK-31 fires ~10s post-fo. A companion CAN in principle spawn within FK-31's window. The timing argument as stated is refutable and should be DOWNGRADED to [I]. What survives independently: flight 10 (fo staging with companion_watch active) observed NO companion spawn during fo injection, but flight 10 also did not reach LVL_Tutorial, so it does not cleanly test the FK-31 window.

Fact 5 [I_strong] — 'Companion observed behavior limited to spawn + terminate' rests on an ETW capture using ONLY PROC_THREAD+LOADER providers (S177 doc line 23). These providers are BLIND BY DESIGN to memory operations (VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect, WriteProcessMemory, NtWriteVirtualMemory, SetThreadContext). The claim 'no WPM activity observed' is technically true but UNINTERPRETABLE — the instrument could not have captured those events even if they occurred. Classic instrument-blind-spot pattern (CLAUDE.md Rule 1). The finding's own open questions acknowledge this: 'One targeted ETW scope with VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect/WriteMemory kernel providers enabled on companion PID would settle this'. Grade should be DOWNGRADED to [I]. The ASCII byte scan for injection API names is also inconclusive because runtime.dll uses import-protection (CLAUDE.md FK-10: 1107/1107 obfuscated import slots), which the finding acknowledges.
notes: Verdict PARTIAL because two [I_strong] facts have real defects requiring downgrade to [I], but the central claim survives because the [M]-graded S168 direct measurement (Fact 3) is decisive on its own. FK-31 attribution to in-process runtime.dll self-check is well-established by S168; supporting arguments in Facts 2 and 5 add less than they claim. Key defects: (a) Fact 2 confuses game-start-to-spawn (50s) with trigger-to-spawn (~5s per flight 9), invalidating the timing argument as stated. Recommend: keep Fact 3 as load-bearing evidence, treat Facts 2 and 5 as [I] supporting arguments; the definitive experiment (one ETW-instrumented staging FK-31 with VirtualAlloc/WriteMemory providers enabled on companion PID) remains cheap and would settle attribution to full [M].
